Column Descriptions: Columns correspond closely with terms listed on page 34 of www.ensembl.org/info/docs/tools/vep/script/VEP_script_documentation.pdf
The chromosome in which the variant occurs
The position in which the variant occurs. Cooridnates map to REFERENCE_GENOME.
Reference Allele in REFERENCE_GENOME
Alternate Allele that occurs in place of the reference allele in the tumor sample

Typically, only PASS variants are added to the excel report. These are variants that pass Mutect2's probability filters. For more info please see: https://github.com/broadinstitute/gatk/blob/master/docs/mutect/mutect.pdf
This is a CCG computed column.  TRUE if BIOTYPE = protein_coding AND (gnomAD_e <= 0.01 OR (gnomADe_AF <= 0.10 AND is in the COSMIC_v104 database)
This is a CCG computed column. Indicates if the variant passes the filtering criteria used in the Variant_Summary_table tab
The type of variant it is: SNV, Indel, etc.
The gene symbol or name based on the BestEffect (most severely affected) transcript
The database the gene symbol or name comes from. HGNC means the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee
The ID number for the Gene in the HGNC Database.
The ID number for the Gene in the Ensemble Database.
What kind of biological entity? The biological function of the RNA (i.e. whether it's protein_coding or regulatory).
The effect for the given variant across the standard/most common transcript.
What kind of genomic feature for the standard/most common sequence? If there is mRNA that derives from DNA, will say 'transcript' in this column
The ID of standard/most common RNA that derives from the DNA.
If the standard/most common transcript of the variant is in an exon, this will have the 'Exon number / Number of total exons'
If the standard/most common transcript of the variant is in an intron, this will have the 'Intron number / Number of total introns'
Relative position of the base pair from the start of the mature, standard, most common transcript (cDNA) sequence.
Relative position of the base pair from the start of the coding sequence for the original DNA based on the standard/most common transcript.
Relative position of the amino acid from the start of the translated protein based on the standard/most common transcript.
The amino acids that were changed by the genetic change based on the standard/most common transcript.
The effect for the given variant across the most severely affected transcript.
What kind of genomic feature for the  most severely affected sequence? If there is mRNA that derives from DNA, will say 'transcript' in this column
The ID of most severely affected RNA that derives from the DNA.
If the most severely affected transcript of the variant is in an exon, this will have the 'Exon number / Number of total exons'
If the most severely affected transcript of the variant is in an intron, this will have the 'Intron number / Number of total introns'
Relative position of the base pair from the start of the mature, most severely affected transcript (cDNA) sequence.
Relative position of the base pair from the start of the coding sequence for the original DNA based on the most severely affected transcript.
Relative position of the amino acid from the start of the translated protein based on the most severely affected transcript.
The amino acids that were changed by the genetic change based on the most severely affected transcript.
Allele Fraction from Mutect2. Mutect2 filters out normal tissue contamination reads.
Depth from Mutect2. Mutect2 filters out normal tissue contamination reads.

The IDs in the following databases that catalogue known variants: dbSNP (start with rs), HGMD (start with CM (Missense/Nonsense), CD (Deletion), or CI (Insertion)). There are other databases that VEP caches too (Cancer Gene Census, ClinVar, dbGaP, dbPEX, dbVar, DGVA, G2P, GEFOS, GenCC, GIANT, Infevers, KAT6BDB, MAGIC, NHGRI-EBI, OIVID, OMIM, Orphanet, PAHdb, PharmGKB, PhenCode, Teslovich, and UniProt); further information is here: https://jun2026.archive.ensembl.org/info/genome/variation/species/sources_documentation.html.
The ID from COSMIC (catalogue of somatic mutations in cancer) version 104. COSV IDs are mapped to one and only one chromosome, position, and variant.
How many times this COSMIC_v104 ID was found in whole genome screens.
How many times this COSMIC_v104 ID was found in targeted panels.
The ID from COSMIC (catalogue of somatic mutations in cancer) version 80. COSM IDs are more disorganized than COSV IDs (mapped sometimes by variant and sometimes by RNA transcript).
How many times this COSMIC_v104 ID was found in any screens.
Frequency of existing variant in 1000 Genomes. This is a renamed column; it corresponds to the AF column in the CSQ section of the .vcf file.
Frequency of existing variant in gnomAD exomes combined population
Frequency of existing variant in gnomAD genomes combined population
Maximum observed allele frequency in 1000 Genomes, ESP and gnomAD
Populations (African/American, Ashkenazi Jewish, East Asian, South Asian, etc.) in which maximum allele frequency was observed.
